title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and notation (continuing p.29). M_{g,ν} is the moduli stack over Q of smooth curves of genus g with ν ordered marked points. \overline{M}_{g,ν} is its geometric fibre over \bar Q: the bar means base change to \bar Q, not the Deligne–Mumford compactification. Γ = Gal(\bar Q/Q). Page 29 gave the fundamental exact sequence 1 → π1(\overline M_{g,ν}) ≅ \hat T_{g,ν} → π1(M_{g,ν}) → Γ → 1, where \hat T_{g,ν} is the profinite completion of the Teichmüller (mapping class) group. It maps to 1 → \hat T_{g,ν} → Autext lac°(\hat π1(X∖{x_1..x_ν})) → Out(..) → 1. Here 'Autext lac' means outer automorphisms of the profinite surface group that respect the conjugacy classes of the loops ('lacets') around the punctures, up to the cyclotomic power. Grothendieck hoped the middle arrow is an isomorphism, which would give an 'anabelian' characterization of Γ.

On this page he passes to N_{g,ν} = M_{g,ν}/S_ν, the moduli of curves with an unordered set of ν points. M_{g,ν} → N_{g,ν} is a Galois étale cover with constant group S_ν, defined over Q and geometrically connected. This yields (5): 1 → π1(\overline M_{g,ν}) → π1(N_{g,ν}) → S_ν × Γ → 1. He reads this as π1(\overline M_{g,ν}) viewed as a profinite group with outer operators by S_ν × Γ. This is an extension structure 'richer' than the first line of (4).

The conjecture is then reformulated with permutations of the punctures allowed:
- π1(N_{g,ν}) ≅ Autext lac(\hat π1(X_ξ∖{x_1..x_ν})), the outer automorphisms preserving the set of inertia classes;
- equivalently Γ ≅ Autext lac(\hat π1)/\hat{\tilde T}_{g,ν}, where \tilde T_{g,ν} is the full mapping class group, which permutes the punctures;
- for comparison, the discrete statement \tilde T_{g,ν} ≅ Autext lac^+(π1^{top}(X∖{x_i})), i.e. orientation-preserving, loop-preserving outer automorphisms of the topological surface group. This is the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem.

NB: he wants the automorphism group G_{g,ν} of the geometric modular stack \overline M_{g,ν}. He guesses G_{g,ν} = S_ν, acting faithfully except for g=0, ν≤4.

Final Question: is Γ → Autext(\hat T_{g,ν}) = Out(π1(\overline M_{g,ν})) injective, or even bijective? He expects conditions on small (g,ν). The next page asks whether Autext of the discrete group π_{g,ν} is trivial.

Purpose: to characterize Γ, and the arithmetic π1 of moduli stacks, purely group-theoretically. One route is via loop-preserving outer automorphisms of profinite surface groups; the other is via outer automorphisms of profinite mapping class groups. This is the program that became the Teichmüller tower / \widehat{GT} part of the Esquisse.
errors: The faithfulness exceptions in the NB look incomplete. For (g,ν)=(1,2), the swap of the two points is 2-isomorphic to the identity on the stack M_{1,2}, via the canonical isomorphism x ↦ p+q−x from (E,p,q) to (E,q,p). So S_2 does not act effectively there either. Trivial cases (ν≤1, (0,3)) aside, the true exception list includes (0,4), where S_4 acts through S_3, and (1,2).

The conjecture is stated uniformly in (g,ν), but it is at best open, and likely false or needing modification for small (g,ν). For (0,3) it would assert Γ×S_3 ≅ inertia-preserving Out(\hat F_2). The later literature needs extra rigidity (M_{0,5}, the tower, GT relations) to reach \widehat{GT}, and even \widehat{GT} = Γ is open. Grothendieck flags conditions on small g,ν only for the final question.
No mathematical error in (5): the quotient π1(N)/π1(\overline M) is indeed S_ν × Γ, because the S_ν-cover M→N is defined over Q and geometrically connected.

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1→π1(\overline M_{g,ν})→π1(N_{g,ν})→S_ν×Γ→1 for the unordered-points moduli stack; π1(\overline M) treated as a profinite group with outer S_ν×Γ-action.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{g,n}/S_n; outer Galois representation on profinite mapping class groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmüller tower discussion (in spirit)

ideas.what: Conjecture: π1(N_{g,ν}) ≅ loop-preserving outer automorphism group of the profinite surface group; equivalently Γ ≅ Autext lac(\hat Π_{g,ν})/\hat{\tilde T}_{g,ν}.
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian / Galois-rigidity characterization of π1 of moduli stacks; inertia-preserving Out of profinite surface groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Injectivity: Belyi, Matsumoto, Hoshi–Mochizuki. Surjectivity-type statements: \widehat{GT} results of Harbater–Schneps, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki, Minamide–Nakamura, Boggi–Funar–Lochak.
ideas.where_published: The idea of recovering Γ as automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower is in Esquisse; this level-by-level Autext lac form is not, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Discrete comparison: \tilde T_{g,ν} ≅ orientation-preserving, puncture-loop-preserving Out of the surface group.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn, Nielsen, Baer; Zieschang for punctured surfaces

ideas.what: Determine the automorphism group of the geometric moduli stack; guess S_ν, acting faithfully except small cases.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism groups of M_{g,n} (and of its compactification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Royden; Earle–Kra (analytic, via Teichmüller space); Bruno–Mella, Massarenti (algebraic, 2010s)

ideas.what: Question: is Γ → Out(\hat T_{g,ν}) injective or bijective (for (g,ν) not too small)? Next page: is Out of the discrete mapping class group trivial?
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on profinite mapping class groups; Out(\hat Γ_{g,n}) vs \widehat{GT}; Ivanov's theorem for discrete Out
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ivanov/McCarthy (discrete Out(Γ_g)≅Z/2); Matsumoto, Hoshi–Mochizuki (injectivity); Harbater–Schneps, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki, Minamide–Nakamura, Boggi–Funar–Lochak (\widehat{GT} descriptions)
ideas.where_published: Closely related to Esquisse's description of Γ via the Teichmüller tower

missed.claim: This is an explicit, dated (c.1980-81) level-by-level formulation of two things. First, a conjecture identifying π1 of each moduli stack N_{g,ν} over Q with the full puncture-set-preserving outer automorphism group of the profinite surface group. Second, the question whether Γ → Out(\hat T_{g,ν}) is bijective. Both predate Esquisse, which instead works with the whole tower. The question anticipates the later program computing Out of profinite braid and mapping class groups (Harbater–Schneps 2000; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki; Minamide–Nakamura; Boggi–Funar–Lochak). There the answer is \widehat{GT}-type rather than Γ, unless \widehat{GT}=Γ.
missed.quote: Question Γ → Autext(\hat T_{g,ν}) injectif? bijectif? (Sans doute il faut conditions sur g, ν petit)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the 'Out of profinite mapping class groups' question, and for the idea of testing Γ against each single level M_{g,ν} rather than the tower. Not a new mathematical result; the mathematics was taken up independently.

missed.claim: Determining the automorphism group of the geometric moduli stack M_{g,ν}⊗\bar Q, with the conjecture that it is S_ν. This was later settled essentially by others: Royden/Earle–Kra analytically, Massarenti and others algebraically. Grothendieck's exception list misses (1,2).
missed.quote: Il faudrait déterminer le groupe des automorphismes G_{g,ν} des types modulaires géom. \overline M_{g,ν} ... sans doute S_ν qui [opère] fidèlement sauf g=0, ν≤4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; confirms that Grothendieck posed the question, which was later answered.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck's interest in Γ acting on the Teichmüller tower is well known from Esquisse. What is mildly notable here is the explicit early question 'Γ → Out(\hat T_{g,ν}) bijective?' and the per-level loop-preserving-Out conjecture with unordered punctures; these foreshadow the 2000s–2010s \widehat{GT} computations. No new theorem is on the page.
transcription_corrections: 'Autextloc' should read 'Autext lac' (lac = lacets, i.e. loop/inertia-preserving), consistent with p.29.
'La conjecture fait équivalente : la suivante' should read approximately 'La conjecture faite équivaut à la suivante'.

'π1(N_{g,ν},ξ) = π1(\overline N_{g,ν}, Γ_?)' is likely 'π1(\overline N_{g,ν}, Γ)'. Likewise the next line is 'π1(\overline M_{g,ν}, S_ν, ξ) = π1(\overline M_{g,ν}, S_ν×Γ)': notation for π1 of the geometric fibre with outer operators.
The NB should read: '... (G_{g,ν} = S_ν ?) sans doute S_ν, qui [opère] fidèlement sauf g=0, ν≤4 ...'. The '{+Id+}' above S_ν is an interlinear alternative ('Id'?).

In the final Question, '\overline{π1(M_{g,ν})}' is written under \hat T_{g,ν} as its gloss: \hat T_{g,ν} = π1(\overline M_{g,ν}). The bracketed words are 'injectif' / 'bijectif', with the parenthesis '(Sans doute il faut conditions sur g, ν petit)'.
The quotient in the 'ou encore' line is by \hat{\tilde T}_{g,ν} (profinite completion of the full mapping class group), not '\tilde T^∧' with a separate superscript.
